# Reference Notes 

Made By Abhik Biswas 

For any power-law potential of the form _V_ ( _r_ ) = _ar_<sup>_k_</sup> (or _V_ ( _x_ ) = _ax_<sup>_k_</sup> in 1D), the **General Virial Theorem** states that the expectation value (or time-average) of kinetic energy _⟨T ⟩_ and potential energy _⟨V ⟩_ are related by: 



<!-- Start of picture text -->
2 ⟨ T ⟩ =  k ⟨ V ⟩<br><!-- End of picture text -->

**General Expressions in Terms of Total Energy** _E_ 

Since total energy is _E_ = _⟨T ⟩_ + _⟨V ⟩_ , we can express both _⟨T ⟩_ and _⟨V ⟩_ directly as fractions of total energy _E_ : 

1. **Kinetic Energy:** 



<!-- Start of picture text -->
2. Potential Energy:<br><!-- End of picture text -->



<!-- Start of picture text -->
k<br>⟨ T ⟩ = E<br>( k  +  2 )<br>2<br>⟨ V ⟩ = E<br>( k  +  2 )<br><!-- End of picture text -->

## **Key Notes to Remember** 

- **For Hydrogen Atom (** _k_ = _−_ 1 **):** Since bound states have negative total energy ( _E <_ 0), the kinetic energy _⟨T ⟩_ = _−E_ is positive, and potential energy _⟨V ⟩_ = 2 _E_ is negative, maintaining _⟨T ⟩_ = _−_<sup><u>1</u></sup> 2<sup>_⟨V ⟩_.</sup> 

- **Quick Shortcut Rule:** As the power _k_ increases, the potential well becomes steeper, trapping the particle more tightly at the edges and allocating a larger share of total energy _E_ to **kinetic energy** _⟨T ⟩_ .
